summary: Claude loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, explicitly classified the "move API endpoint config into a settings module" brief as ARCHITECTURAL, ran clarifying question rounds, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-26-api-settings-module-design.md, presented it for review, and only after "looks good, go ahead" moved to writing-plans. No implementation code was written before approval.
reasoning: Every acceptance criterion was met with direct evidence from the session log, the on-disk spec file, git status, and the terminal screen. The only notable defect was the non-functional Codex review stub, which is outside the graded criteria and was handled transparently by the agent.

observations.description: The Codex spec review gate produced no usable result: "Both round-1 lenses (completeness-and-consistency, feasibility-and-scope) returned an empty payload; verdict-normalize --require-coverage returned incomplete for each ... status --json shows no job was ever registered (running: [], latestFinished: null) ... installed companion reports version 0.0.0-stub". The agent handled it gracefully and recorded an ungated-review event, but the seeded Codex stub yields zero independent review value.

The multi-question approval form (tabs Approve / Tooling / Submit) with checkbox groups plus a separate 'Submit' row and then a 'Submit answers' confirmation is several keystroke layers deep; easy for a user to think their answer was submitted when it wasn't.
The approval option text offers 'Yes, but skip the spec doc' right after the agent declared the task architectural, which invites the user to undo the classification the skill just made.
Agent offered up-front 'Say the word if you'd rather I collapse this to a quick in-chat design' — honest, but it nudges toward downgrading the architectural path.
Spec used placeholder URLs (localhost:3000, staging-api.example.com, staging.example.com) invented without asking; agent flagged them, but these guesses could have been a clarifying question instead.

criteria.evidence: Session log grep: `grep -o 'hyperpowers:[a-z-]*' <session>.jsonl | sort | uniq -c` → "67 hyperpowers:brainstorming"; screen also showed Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) loaded only after spec approval.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec to docs/*/specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: First assistant text in log: "**Classification: architectural.** Normally a one-constant move would be bounded, but the request names a module this repo doesn't have...". File on disk: coding-agent-workdir/docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-26-api-settings-module-design.md, beginning "# API Settings Module — Design ... Status: awaiting user review".

criteria.criterion: Spec surfaced for review and approval before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-26-api-settings-module-design.md (not committed). Please review it before I write the implementation plan." After my "looks good, go ahead": "Spec approved. Invoking the writing-plans skill". `git status --short` in workdir showed only "?? docs/" — no source files modified.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip the spec
criteria.evidence: Agent announced "Classification: architectural" and produced a committed-to-disk spec file; the approval menu even offered "Yes, but skip the spec doc" which was not taken (review summary showed "→ looks good, go ahead" and spec was written).

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / probe plan
criteria.evidence: No probe plan appeared; log grep of assistant text for 'spike' returned no classification statement (only the architectural line matched), and the flow went questions → design → spec → plan.
